gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a working camera-plus-gate-release setup costs over a year. The JAGER PRO DIY Conversion Kit (camera, control box, latch and remote) costs $2,280 in year one ($1,800 + 12 × $40 live-video plan) and $480 a year after that. Hog Trap Trigger's $999 solar trigger includes its first year of cell service and renews for $125 a year, but you have to add your own camera and that camera's plan.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited (jagerpro.com M.I.N.E. Live Stream product page, hogtraptrigger.com home page, hogeyecameras.com home page) and the top JAGER PRO results. The JAGER product page gives a $599 camera-only price and a data-plan line, but no gate-included total and no annual figure. Its plan line reads "$40/month (up to 5GB)", while ChatGPT told the shopper $55/month. The hogtraptrigger.com home page has no prices at all; they are only on its /shop/ page, which ChatGPT did not get. HogEye publishes no prices on its home, buy-now or steel-camera pages. None of these pages adds hardware and 12 months of plan into a first-year cost, or compares the yearly cost after that.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's own follow-up question about whether the shopper already has a trap. For someone with an existing trap, the cheaper recurring path is a separate trigger plus any cellular camera: Hog Trap Trigger at $125/yr, plus for example AnywhereCam's $18.67/mo plan, which is $224.04/yr, for $349.04/yr in total. JAGER's integrated system costs $480/yr in plan fees alone. A JAGER buyer who wants live video and a gate release needs the $1,800 kit, not the $599 camera, so they should budget $2,280 for year one. It also fixes ChatGPT's plan price: the maker's pages say $40/mo, not $55.
